methodology_notes:
Two items were genuinely close calls and could reasonably be scored the other way by another judge.

Item 4 (severity ranking): X and Y both present findings as a numbered list without HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW tags. I scored Y present because it carries an explicit heading, "Findings, worst first," which is a direct textual claim that the ordering is severity-based. I scored X absent because it has no equivalent heading or ranking statement — only bare numbering ("## 1." … "## 8.") plus one incidental remark that defects 1–2 are "the worst outcome available here." A stricter reading that required explicit HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW labels (as W and Z use) would mark Y absent too, collapsing X and Y to the same score on this item.

Item 6 (receipts for clean axes): X's "What the note got right" section and Y's "On the producer's note" section are structurally the same move (auditing the producer's claims) and are the closest either output gets to receipts. I scored X present because its SQL-injection and error-body lines each name the specific mechanism checked ("$1 with a value array"; "detail going to logger, not the response"). I scored Y absent because its equivalent lines are closer to bare re-assertions ("correct. There is no injection") without restating the mechanism. This line is genuinely thin, and a reader who treats both sections as equivalent-effort commentary rather than dedicated verification receipts could mark X absent too — I did not find a clean-axis receipt section as explicit as W's or Z's dedicated "How each clean axis was checked" heading in either X or Y.

Item 1 (tri-state verdict): I required an actual three-state vocabulary (or a single one of the three labels, implying the schema) rather than any strong verdict sentence. X's "does not meet the contract. Do not merge." and Y's "fails the contract. Do not merge." are unambiguous binary/prose conclusions by that standard, so I did not treat forcefulness of language as a substitute for the tri-state marker.

Also flagged as substantive rather than checklist-mechanical: Y's claim that the contract has "four clauses" is inconsistent with W's and X's three-clause framing of the same contract. I could not verify which count is correct since the underlying contract text is not included in this bundle — I noted it as a discrepancy rather than a confirmed error.
